**2. BACKGROUND AND BUSINESS JUSTIFICATION**

MWCPU currently receives claims through three separate channels: (1) a shared Excel workbook maintained by the intake desk, (2) emailed PDF intake forms from agents, and (3) an older IntakeTrack web form that is no longer vendor-supported. This fragmented intake process has produced the following issues:

- Duplicate claim numbers assigned to the same incident (12 confirmed duplicates in Q4 2023).
- Average intake processing time of 4.2 business days, exceeding the unit's 2-day service standard.
- Manual data entry errors in policy number and date-of-loss fields, requiring rework by downstream examiners.
- No centralized audit trail for intake changes.

ClaimIntake Pro addresses these issues by providing:

- **Automated duplicate detection** using policy number + date of loss + claimant last name matching logic.
- **Real-time validation** against the policy administration system (PAS) for policy status and coverage codes.
- **Configurable intake forms** with conditional fields based on line of business.
- **Document attachment and OCR** for PDF and image submissions.
- **Dashboard and reporting** for intake volume and aging metrics.
- **Role-based access control** integrated with Active Directory.

The system was selected through a competitive evaluation of three vendors (RFP 2023-118) and was approved by the IT Steering Committee on December 14, 2023 (Minutes Item 7.3).

---

**5. TECHNICAL CONFIGURATION**

**5.1 System Architecture**
**5.1 System Architecture**

ClaimIntake Pro is deployed as a three-tier application within the MWCPU network environment:

- **Presentation tier:** Web-based interface accessible via the corporate intranet. Supported browsers are Chrome (version 120 or later) and Edge (version 120 or later). No client-side installation is required.
- **Application tier:** Two application servers (CIP-APP01, CIP-APP02) running behind a load balancer. The application servers host the intake workflow engine, validation rules, and the integration adapters for PAS and DMS.
- **Data tier:** SQL Server 2022 database (CIP-DB01) with automatic failover to a secondary replica (CIP-DB02) in the alternate data center. Database backups run nightly at 11:00 PM CT; transaction log backups run every 15 minutes.

Connection strings are stored in the application configuration files, encrypted using the corporate key management service. Service accounts have been provisioned with least-privilege access:

| Service Account | Purpose | Access Scope |
|---|---|---|
| CIP_APP_SVC | Application pool identity | Read/write to CIP database; read-only to PAS lookup tables |
| CIP_INT_SVC | Integration service identity | Read/write to DMS REST API; read-only to PAS policy API |
| CIP_MIG_SVC | Data migration service identity | Read-only to IntakeTrack export files; write to CIP staging tables |

**5.2 Integration Specifications**

The PAS integration is a synchronous web service call initiated when an intake record is created or when policy verification is requested. The system sends the policy number and insured name to the PAS policy verification endpoint. The response includes policy status (Active, Cancelled, Expired, or Not Found), effective dates, and coverage codes. If the response cannot be obtained within 10 seconds, the request is queued for retry (up to three attempts at 5-minute intervals). Records where policy verification fails are flagged as "Pending Verification" and do not move to assignment until resolved.

The DMS integration is asynchronous. After an intake record is saved, the system generates a document index file containing the claim number, document type, and file path. The index file is transmitted to the DMS via a monitored folder. The DMS returns a confirmation message with a document ID; the intake record is updated with the document ID and the document status is set to "Indexed."

## 6. Post-Implementation Review

### 6.1 Go-Live Summary

ClaimIntake Pro went live on March 4, 2024, as planned. The implementation window began at 6:00 PM CT on Friday, March 1, and was completed by 2:15 AM CT on Saturday, March 2. The additional time between completion and the Monday go-live was used for controlled validation of migrated data and final user access checks.

The go-live was declared successful at 8:30 AM CT on March 4 after the first wave of live intake records processed without system errors. A hypercare team of five IT staff members and two MWCPU Business Analysts was on-site (and available remotely) for the first two weeks. Hypercare was extended by one week for the Property line of business due to the assignment rule issue described in Section 6.3.

### 6.2 System Performance Metrics

Performance data was collected from March 4 through April 30, 2024. The table below summarizes key metrics compared to the pre-implementation baseline (average of October 2023 through February 2024).

| Metric | Baseline (Pre-Implementation) | Post-Implementation (Mar 4 – Apr 30) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Average intake record creation time | 14.2 minutes | 6.8 minutes | -52% |
| Average policy verification time | 8.5 minutes (manual lookup) | 1.9 minutes (automated) | -78% |
| Average time from intake to assignment | 26.4 hours | 11.3 hours | -57% |
| Percentage of records with missing or incomplete data at assignment | 11.4% | 4.2% | -63% |
| Percentage of records requiring manual re-entry or correction | 9.8% | 2.1% | -79% |
| System uptime (business hours) | N/A | 99.6% | N/A |
| Average response time (intake screen load) | N/A | 1.7 seconds | N/A |

The most significant improvement was observed in the time from intake to assignment, which dropped from an average of 26.4 hours to 11.3 hours. This reduction is attributed primarily to the automated policy verification and the elimination of the manual data entry step that previously required intake specialists to re-type information from paper forms and email submissions.

Figure 6-1 (see Appendix C) shows the weekly trend of intake-to-assignment time. The metric stabilized at approximately 10–11 hours by the third week of March and remained consistent through April, with the exception of a brief increase to 14.2 hours during the week of April 8–12, which coincided with the policy verification integration issue described below.

### 6.3 Issues Encountered and Resolution

#### Issue 1: Assignment Rule Failure for Property Claims (Severity 2)

**Date Reported:** March 6, 2024  
**Date Resolved:** March 13, 2024  
**Status:** Resolved – Permanent fix deployed

On March 6, it was identified that 23 Property claims received between March 4 and March 6 were not assigned to adjusters within the expected timeframe. Investigation revealed that the assignment rule for Property line of business was referencing a territory code table that had not been fully migrated from the legacy IntakeTrack system. The migration script for this table had been excluded from the final run due to a naming convention mismatch (the legacy table was named `TERR_CODES` while the migration utility expected `TERRITORY_CODES`).

**Immediate action:** IT – Data Services ran a manual script to populate the territory code table from the legacy system backup. This resolved the rule failure for new claims. The 23 affected claims were manually assigned by the Property supervisor on March 7.

**A. Acknowledgment of Claims**

- Upon receipt of a notice of claim, an insurer or TPA must send a written acknowledgment to the claimant within **ten (10) calendar days** of receipt. The acknowledgment must include the claim number, the name and contact information of the person assigned to handle the claim, and a general description of the next steps in the claims process.
- If the claim is received through a licensed producer or agent, the acknowledgment period begins on the date the insurer or TPA receives the notice from the producer or agent, not the date of the initial loss.

**B. Investigation and Communication**

- An insurer or TPA must complete a reasonable investigation of a claim within **thirty (30) calendar days** of receipt of the notice of claim, unless circumstances beyond the control of the insurer or TPA require additional time. Such circumstances must be documented in the claim file.
- The insurer or TPA must provide the claimant with a status update at least every **fifteen (15) calendar days** until a final decision on the claim is made. Status updates may be provided by telephone, email, or written correspondence, provided that the claimant has consented to receive updates by telephone or email.
- Any request for additional information from the claimant must be made in writing and must specifically identify the documents or other information needed and the reason the information is necessary to evaluate the claim. A request for additional information does not suspend the investigation timeline unless the requested information is reasonably necessary to make a coverage determination.

- Any denial of a claim must include a specific explanation of the policy provisions, facts, or other grounds upon which the denial is based. The explanation must be sufficient to allow the claimant to understand the basis for the denial and to pursue any available remedies.

Documentation created before the effective date need not be recreated, provided that the existing documentation is sufficient to support the coverage determination under the standards of this Bulletin. Where the existing documentation is insufficient, the insurer or TPA shall supplement the claim file within thirty (30) calendar days of the effective date.

**B. Transitional Provisions for Third-Party Administrators**

Where a TPA has been engaged by an insurer to handle claims, the insurer remains responsible for ensuring that the TPA's documentation practices comply with this Bulletin. By June 15, 2024, insurers shall obtain from each TPA a written certification that the TPA has updated its procedures and trained its personnel. The certification must be signed by an officer of the TPA and retained in the insurer's records. Insurers that use a TPA and do not obtain such a certification by the deadline may be subject to penalties for noncompliance.

**C. Compliance Reporting**

On or before August 1, 2024, each insurer shall submit to the Commission a one-time compliance report. The report must include:

1. The name and contact information of the individual designated as the primary compliance contact for this Bulletin;
2. A summary of the gap assessment completed pursuant to Section V.A, including a description of any gaps identified and the corrective actions taken;
3. The date on which internal policy and procedure updates were completed;
4. A statement confirming that all claims personnel have completed the required training, along with the number of personnel trained; and
5. A list of any TPAs used by the insurer for claims handling, with a notation of whether each TPA provided the certification required by Section V.B.

**Subject:** Documentation Standards for Property and Casualty Claims Handling

**Issued:** April 10, 2024
**Effective Date:** July 1, 2024

---

**VI. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS**

The following questions were compiled from inquiries received by the Commission following the issuance of the draft version of this Bulletin. These responses are intended to provide general guidance and do not constitute legal advice or a substitute for consultation with counsel.

**Q1: Does this Bulletin apply to claims handled under a self-insured retention or a captive insurance arrangement?**

A: No. This Bulletin applies to insurers and third-party administrators (TPAs) licensed or otherwise authorized to transact business in Illinois for property and casualty lines of insurance. A self-insured retention is not an insurance policy, and a captive insurer that is not admitted in Illinois is not subject to this Bulletin. However, if an admitted insurer issues a policy with a self-insured retention, the insurer remains responsible for the documentation standards set forth herein for its portion of the claim handling.

**Q2: Our company uses a hybrid model where some adjusters are employees and others are independent contractors. How does the training requirement in Section IV apply to independent contractor adjusters?**

A: The training requirement applies to all individuals who perform claims handling functions on behalf of the insurer, regardless of their employment or contractor status. For independent contractor adjusters, the insurer must verify that the adjuster has completed training that meets the standards of Section IV. This may be accomplished by requiring the contractor to provide a certificate of completion, or by the insurer providing the training directly. The insurer is responsible for maintaining documentation of this verification for each contractor adjuster.

**Q3: Section III.A requires a "contemporaneous record" of the claim. Does this mean that our adjusters can no longer draft their notes after a phone call and then enter them into the system at the end of the day?**

A: The Commission understands that adjusters often take notes during a conversation and then formalize them into the claim file. A contemporaneous record is one that is created at the time of the event or as soon as practically possible thereafter, and that accurately reflects the substance of the communication or activity. A record created at the end of the business day that captures the details of a call made that morning would generally be considered contemporaneous. A record created several days later, or one that is reconstructed from memory, would not.

**Q4: Does the requirement to document the "basis for the coverage determination" in Section III.B require us to include a full legal analysis in every claim file?**

A: No. The requirement is intended to ensure that the claim file contains enough information to explain why a particular coverage decision was made. For a straightforward claim, this may be a brief notation referencing the applicable policy provision. For a more complex claim involving ambiguous policy language or a dispute over facts, a more detailed explanation would be expected. The level of detail should be proportionate to the complexity of the decision.

**2. BACKGROUND AND BUSINESS JUSTIFICATION**

MWCPU currently receives claims through three separate channels: (1) a shared Excel workbook maintained by the intake desk, (2) emailed PDF intake forms from agents, and (3) an older IntakeTrack web form that is no longer vendor-supported. This fragmented intake process has produced the following issues:

- Duplicate claim numbers assigned to the same incident (12 confirmed duplicates in Q4 2023).
- Average intake processing time of 4.2 business days, exceeding the unit's 2-day service standard.
- Manual data entry errors in policy number and date-of-loss fields, requiring rework by downstream examiners.
- No centralized audit trail for intake changes.

ClaimIntake Pro addresses these issues by providing:

- **Automated duplicate detection** using policy number + date of loss + claimant last name matching logic.
- **Real-time validation** against the policy administration system (PAS) for policy status and coverage codes.
- **Configurable intake forms** with conditional fields based on line of business.
- **Document attachment and OCR** for PDF and image submissions.
- **Dashboard and reporting** for intake volume and aging metrics.
- **Role-based access control** integrated with Active Directory.

The system was selected through a competitive evaluation of three vendors (RFP 2023-118) and was approved by the IT Steering Committee on December 14, 2023 (Minutes Item 7.3).

**5.1 System Architecture**

ClaimIntake Pro is deployed as a three-tier application within the MWCPU network environment:

- **Presentation tier:** Web-based interface accessible via the corporate intranet. Supported browsers are Chrome (version 120 or later) and Edge (version 120 or later). No client-side installation is required.
- **Application tier:** Two application servers (CIP-APP01, CIP-APP02) running behind a load balancer. The application servers host the intake workflow engine, validation rules, and the integration adapters for PAS and DMS.
- **Data tier:** SQL Server 2022 database (CIP-DB01) with automatic failover to a secondary replica (CIP-DB02) in the alternate data center. Database backups run nightly at 11:00 PM CT; transaction log backups run every 15 minutes.

Connection strings are stored in the application configuration files, encrypted using the corporate key management service. Service accounts have been provisioned with least-privilege access:

| Service Account | Purpose | Access Scope |
|---|---|---|
| CIP_APP_SVC | Application pool identity | Read/write to CIP database; read-only to PAS lookup tables |
| CIP_INT_SVC | Integration service identity | Read/write to DMS REST API; read-only to PAS policy API |
| CIP_MIG_SVC | Data migration service identity | Read-only to IntakeTrack export files; write to CIP staging tables |

**5.2 Integration Specifications**

The PAS integration is a synchronous web service call initiated when an intake record is created or when policy verification is requested. The system sends the policy number and insured name to the PAS policy verification endpoint. The response includes policy status (Active, Cancelled, Expired, or Not Found), effective dates, and coverage codes. If the response cannot be obtained within 10 seconds, the request is queued for retry (up to three attempts at 5-minute intervals). Records where policy verification fails are flagged as "Pending Verification" and do not move to assignment until resolved.

The DMS integration is asynchronous. After an intake record is saved, the system generates a document index file containing the claim number, document type, and file path. The index file is transmitted to the DMS via a monitored folder. The DMS returns a confirmation message with a document ID; the intake record is updated with the document ID and the document status is set to "Indexed."

**5.3 Data Migration Details**

The data migration of open intake records from the Excel workbook and IntakeTrack was performed by IT – Data Services using a series of SQL scripts and a custom migration utility. Key details:

UAT was conducted from February 12 to February 23, 2024. Testing scenarios were prepared by MWCPU Business Analysts and executed by a team of 12 testers (representing Auto, Property, and General Liability lines). The test plan (UAT-CIP-2024-001) included 86 test cases covering:

## 6. Post-Implementation Review

### 6.1 Go-Live Summary

ClaimIntake Pro went live on March 4, 2024, as planned. The implementation window began at 6:00 PM CT on Friday, March 1, and was completed by 2:15 AM CT on Saturday, March 2. The additional time between completion and the Monday go-live was used for controlled validation of migrated data and final user access checks.

The go-live was declared successful at 8:30 AM CT on March 4 after the first wave of live intake records processed without system errors. A hypercare team of five IT staff members and two MWCPU Business Analysts was on-site (and available remotely) for the first two weeks. Hypercare was extended by one week for the Property line of business due to the assignment rule issue described in Section 6.3.

### 6.2 System Performance Metrics

Performance data was collected from March 4 through April 30, 2024. The table below summarizes key metrics compared to the pre-implementation baseline (average of October 2023 through February 2024).

| Metric | Baseline (Pre-Implementation) | Post-Implementation (Mar 4 – Apr 30) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Average intake record creation time | 14.2 minutes | 6.8 minutes | -52% |
| Average policy verification time | 8.5 minutes (manual lookup) | 1.9 minutes (automated) | -78% |
| Average time from intake to assignment | 26.4 hours | 11.3 hours | -57% |
| Percentage of records with missing or incomplete data at assignment | 11.4% | 4.2% | -63% |
| Percentage of records requiring manual re-entry or correction | 9.8% | 2.1% | -79% |
| System uptime (business hours) | N/A | 99.6% | N/A |
| Average response time (intake screen load) | N/A | 1.7 seconds | N/A |

The most significant improvement was observed in the time from intake to assignment, which dropped from an average of 26.4 hours to 11.3 hours. This reduction is attributed primarily to the automated policy verification and the elimination of the manual data entry step that previously required intake specialists to re-type information from paper forms and email submissions.

Figure 6-1 (see Appendix C) shows the weekly trend of intake-to-assignment time. The metric stabilized at approximately 10–11 hours by the third week of March and remained consistent through April, with the exception of a brief increase to 14.2 hours during the week of April 8–12, which coincided with the policy verification integration issue described below.

### 6.3 Issues Encountered and Resolution

#### Issue 1: Assignment Rule Failure for Property Claims (Severity 2)

**Date Reported:** March 6, 2024  
**Date Resolved:** March 13, 2024  
**Status:** Resolved – Permanent fix deployed

On March 6, it was identified that 23 Property claims received between March 4 and March 6 were not assigned to adjusters within the expected timeframe. Investigation revealed that the assignment rule for Property line of business was referencing a territory code table that had not been fully migrated from the legacy IntakeTrack system. The migration script for this table had been excluded from the final run due to a naming convention mismatch (the legacy table was named `TERR_CODES` while the migration utility expected `TERRITORY_CODES`).

**Immediate action:** IT – Data Services ran a manual script to populate the territory code table from the legacy system backup. This resolved the rule failure for new claims. The 23 affected claims were manually assigned by the Property supervisor on March 7.

The regulation applies to all insurers licensed to transact property and casualty insurance in the State of Illinois, including surplus lines insurers operating under the Illinois Surplus Lines Law, and to third-party administrators acting on behalf of such insurers. It does not apply to workers' compensation claims, which remain subject to the Illinois Workers' Compensation Act and related regulations, nor to life, health, or disability income claims, which are governed by separate statutory and regulatory timelines.

The effective date of this regulation is **July 1, 2024**. All insurers and TPAs subject to the regulation must achieve full compliance with its provisions on or before that date. No extension of the effective date will be granted.

**II. STATUTORY AUTHORITY**

This regulation is adopted pursuant to Sections 401 and 403 of the Illinois Insurance Code (215 ILCS 5/401 and 5/403), and Section 154.5 of the Illinois Administrative Procedure Act (5 ILCS 100/154.5). Nothing in this regulation shall be construed to expand, limit, or otherwise alter any duty or obligation imposed by the Illinois Insurance Code or by common law.

**III. KEY REQUIREMENTS**

The regulation establishes the following minimum standards. A complete copy of the regulation text is available on the Commission's website at www.insurance.il.gov/regulations/IL-R-2024-017.pdf.

The State Insurance Commission of Illinois issued_regulation IL-R-2024-017 in the regulatory bulletin. Record status: current.

**A. Acknowledgment of Claims**

- Upon receipt of a notice of claim, an insurer or TPA must send a written acknowledgment to the claimant within **ten (10) calendar days** of receipt. The acknowledgment must include the claim number, the name and contact information of the person assigned to handle the claim, and a general description of the next steps in the claims process.
- If the claim is received through a licensed producer or agent, the acknowledgment period begins on the date the insurer or TPA receives the notice from the producer or agent, not the date of the initial loss.

**B. Investigation and Communication**

- An insurer or TPA must complete a reasonable investigation of a claim within **thirty (30) calendar days** of receipt of the notice of claim, unless circumstances beyond the control of the insurer or TPA require additional time. Such circumstances must be documented in the claim file.
- The insurer or TPA must provide the claimant with a status update at least every **fifteen (15) calendar days** until a final decision on the claim is made. Status updates may be provided by telephone, email, or written correspondence, provided that the claimant has consented to receive updates by telephone or email.
- Any request for additional information from the claimant must be made in writing and must specifically identify the documents or other information needed and the reason the information is necessary to evaluate the claim. A request for additional information does not suspend the investigation timeline unless the requested information is reasonably necessary to make a coverage determination.

**C. Decision on the Claim**

- A decision to approve or deny a claim must be communicated to the claimant in writing within **forty-five (45) calendar days** of receipt of the notice of claim, unless the investigation timeline has been extended as permitted under Section III.B above. In the event of an extension, the decision must be communicated no later than fifteen (15) calendar days after the investigation is completed, and in no event later than ninety (90) calendar days after receipt of the notice of claim.
- Any denial of a claim must include a specific explanation of the policy provisions, facts, or other grounds upon which the denial is based. The explanation must be sufficient to allow the claimant to understand the basis for the denial and to pursue any available remedies.

ILLINOIS STATE INSURANCE COMMISSION
Regulatory Bulletin IL-R-2024-017
Subject: Claims Handling Documentation Standards for Property and Casualty Insurers and Third-Party Administrators
Date of Issue: May 15, 2024
Effective Date: July 1, 2024
Reference: 50 Ill. Adm. Code 910.20; 215 ILCS 5/154.5

---

**Section V. Implementation Timeline and Transitional Provisions**

Insurers and third-party administrators (TPAs) subject to this Bulletin must achieve full compliance with the documentation standards set forth in Sections II through IV no later than the effective date of July 1, 2024. The Commission recognizes that certain operational adjustments—particularly those involving file retention systems, personnel training, and vendor oversight—require lead time. Accordingly, the following implementation schedule applies:

| Milestone | Deadline | Required Action |
|---|---|---|
| Internal gap assessment | June 1, 2024 | Each insurer and TPA shall complete a written assessment of its current claims documentation practices against the standards in this Bulletin. The assessment must identify any gaps and be retained for Commission review. |
| Policy and procedure updates | June 15, 2024 | Updates to internal claims handling manuals, desk procedures, and quality assurance checklists must be finalized and distributed to all relevant personnel. |
| Training completion | June 25, 2024 | All claims personnel, including adjusters, supervisors, and quality assurance staff, must complete training on the new documentation requirements. Training records must be maintained. |
| Full compliance | July 1, 2024 | All claims opened on or after this date must be handled in accordance with this Bulletin. Claims already in progress as of this date are subject to the transitional provisions below. |

**A. Transitional Provisions for Claims in Progress**

For claims that were opened prior to July 1, 2024, and remain open on that date, insurers and TPAs shall apply the documentation standards of this Bulletin to all new documentation created on or after the effective date. Documentation created before the effective date need not be recreated, provided that the existing documentation is sufficient to support the coverage determination under the standards of this Bulletin. Where the existing documentation is insufficient, the insurer or TPA shall supplement the claim file within thirty (30) calendar days of the effective date.

**B. Transitional Provisions for Third-Party Administrators**

Where a TPA has been engaged by an insurer to handle claims, the insurer remains responsible for ensuring that the TPA's documentation practices comply with this Bulletin. By June 15, 2024, insurers shall obtain from each TPA a written certification that the TPA has updated its procedures and trained its personnel. The certification must be signed by an officer of the TPA and retained in the insurer's records. Insurers that use a TPA and do not obtain such a certification by the deadline may be subject to penalties for noncompliance.

**C. Compliance Reporting**

On or before August 1, 2024, each insurer shall submit to the Commission a one-time compliance report. The report must include:

1. The name and contact information of the individual designated as the primary compliance contact for this Bulletin;
2. A summary of the gap assessment completed pursuant to Section V.A, including a description of any gaps identified and the corrective actions taken;
3. The date on which internal policy and procedure updates were completed;
4. A statement confirming that all claims personnel have completed the required training, along with the number of personnel trained; and
5. A list of any TPAs used by the insurer for claims handling, with a notation of whether each TPA provided the certification required by Section V.B.

STATE OF ILLINOIS
DEPARTMENT OF INSURANCE AND FINANCIAL REGULATION
SPRINGFIELD, ILLINOIS

---

**REGULATORY BULLETIN IL-R-2024-017**

**Subject:** Documentation Standards for Property and Casualty Claims Handling

**Issued:** April 10, 2024
**Effective Date:** July 1, 2024

---

**VI. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS**

The following questions were compiled from inquiries received by the Commission following the issuance of the draft version of this Bulletin. These responses are intended to provide general guidance and do not constitute legal advice or a substitute for consultation with counsel.

**Q1: Does this Bulletin apply to claims handled under a self-insured retention or a captive insurance arrangement?**

A: No. This Bulletin applies to insurers and third-party administrators (TPAs) licensed or otherwise authorized to transact business in Illinois for property and casualty lines of insurance. A self-insured retention is not an insurance policy, and a captive insurer that is not admitted in Illinois is not subject to this Bulletin. However, if an admitted insurer issues a policy with a self-insured retention, the insurer remains responsible for the documentation standards set forth herein for its portion of the claim handling.

**Q2: Our company uses a hybrid model where some adjusters are employees and others are independent contractors. How does the training requirement in Section IV apply to independent contractor adjusters?**

A: The training requirement applies to all individuals who perform claims handling functions on behalf of the insurer, regardless of their employment or contractor status. For independent contractor adjusters, the insurer must verify that the adjuster has completed training that meets the standards of Section IV. This may be accomplished by requiring the contractor to provide a certificate of completion, or by the insurer providing the training directly. The insurer is responsible for maintaining documentation of this verification for each contractor adjuster.

**Q3: Section III.A requires a "contemporaneous record" of the claim. Does this mean that our adjusters can no longer draft their notes after a phone call and then enter them into the system at the end of the day?**

A: The Commission understands that adjusters often take notes during a conversation and then formalize them into the claim file. A contemporaneous record is one that is created at the time of the event or as soon as practically possible thereafter, and that accurately reflects the substance of the communication or activity. A record created at the end of the business day that captures the details of a call made that morning would generally be considered contemporaneous. A record created several days later, or one that is reconstructed from memory, would not.

**Q4: Does the requirement to document the "basis for the coverage determination" in Section III.B require us to include a full legal analysis in every claim file?**

A: No. The requirement is intended to ensure that the claim file contains enough information to explain why a particular coverage decision was made. For a straightforward claim, this may be a brief notation referencing the applicable policy provision. For a more complex claim involving ambiguous policy language or a dispute over facts, a more detailed explanation would be expected. The level of detail should be proportionate to the complexity of the decision.
